headline: 15,393 passengers stranded as 100 flights to Saudi Arabia disrupted
summary: Operational restrictions at Saudi airports following Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport have led to widespread flight cancellations and suspensions.
details: Over 15,393 passengers have been left stranded as 100 flights on direct and transit routes between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia were disrupted.
The disruptions were caused by operational restrictions at Saudi airports following Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the affected flights include 41 direct and 59 transit flights.
Among direct flights, Biman Bangladesh Airlines had 17 flights, US-Bangla Airlines 10, Saudia 7, and Riyadh Air 7 disrupted.
Transit flights affected include those from IndiGo (22), Emirates (14), Salam Air (7), Qatar Airways (7), flydubai (6), Air India (2), and EgyptAir (1).
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended all flights to Riyadh and Dammam until October 17, while US-Bangla Airlines has cancelled all Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights until October 21.
caption:
Over 15,000 passengers stranded! 100 flights to Saudi Arabia disrupted following Houthi attacks on a Riyadh airport.

Over 15,393 passengers have been left stranded as 100 flights on direct and transit routes between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia were disrupted.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the affected flights include 41 direct and 59 transit flights.

Among direct flights, Biman Bangladesh Airlines had 17 flights, US-Bangla Airlines 10, Saudia 7, and Riyadh Air 7 disrupted.

Transit flights affected include those from IndiGo (22), Emirates (14), Salam Air (7), Qatar Airways (7), flydubai (6), Air India (2), and EgyptAir (1).

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended all flights to Riyadh and Dammam until October 17, while US-Bangla Airlines has cancelled all Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights until October 21.

headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being trafficked
summary: Victims were allegedly recruited for construction jobs but forced to fight in the war after 21 days of training, according to the Special Response Battalion.
details: Twenty of 30 Bangladeshis allegedly recruited for construction jobs in Russia have been killed after being forced to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war, the Special Response Battalion (SRB) says.
Seventeen died in a drone strike on their first day at the front, with three others dying later, according to Additional DIG Asaduzzaman, commander of SRB-10.
The investigation began after Rajon Hossain, 21, returned home wounded. He had been charged Tk 825,000 for a promised construction job.
Rajon reported that after arriving in Russia on May 7, he and about 30 others were forced into the Russian Army and given 21 days of training before being sent to the front.
A drone strike fractured Rajon's pelvis, leaving him unable to move his legs. He crawled nearly four kilometers to reach a camp and eventually escaped with embassy assistance.
Two alleged recruiters, Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher Lentu, were arrested on Tuesday. Investigators say the network operated through companies including Jabal-e-Nur, RS International, and TS Group.
The SRB reports that two returnees are recovering in Bangladesh, two others are in a Moscow hospital, and six are still on the battlefield.
caption:
Trafficked under the guise of construction jobs, 20 Bangladeshis were forced into the Russian Army and killed in the war.

Twenty of 30 Bangladeshis allegedly recruited for construction jobs in Russia have been killed after being forced to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war, the Special Response Battalion (SRB) says.

Seventeen died in a drone strike on their first day at the front, with three others dying later, according to Additional DIG Asaduzzaman, commander of SRB-10.

The investigation began after Rajon Hossain, 21, returned home wounded. He had been charged Tk 825,000 for a promised construction job.

Rajon reported that after arriving in Russia on May 7, he and about 30 others were forced into the Russian Army and given 21 days of training before being sent to the front.

A drone strike fractured Rajon's pelvis, leaving him unable to move his legs. He crawled nearly four kilometers to reach a camp and eventually escaped with embassy assistance.

Two alleged recruiters, Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher Lentu, were arrested on Tuesday. Investigators say the network operated through companies including Jabal-e-Nur, RS International, and TS Group.

The SRB reports that two returnees are recovering in Bangladesh, two others are in a Moscow hospital, and six are still on the battlefield.
